clues: A big city in Morocco stands on the Atlantic shore at the foot of the Atlas Mountains. It sits just north of where a river flows into the sea.
This shore town holds a heat mark past fifty degrees, set in the year 1940 and still in doubt today. Few coast towns in the world share such a mark.
In 1911, a sharp crisis here laid bare the strain between France and Germany. It was a clear sign of the world war soon to come.
A quake wiped out this city in 1960, and it was built again from scratch. New rules forced builders to make each block quake safe.
It is famed as the chief home of Amazigh culture in Morocco. Most of its folk speak the old local tongue in daily life.
